descripcion_es: Asking for clarification, agreeing or disagreeing, qualifying and concluding.
resumen: Phrases for taking part in a debate or in an examining board’s question time: asking for clarification, agreeing or disagreeing politely, conceding, qualifying, interrupting and closing an answer.

explicacion.texto: In English, direct disagreement (“You are wrong”) sounds abrupt. The usual approach is to soften it: acknowledge part of the argument and then introduce the objection (“I see your point, but…”). In front of an examining board, it is also a good idea to confirm that you have understood the question.

filas: Could you clarify what you mean by…?
Could you clarify what you mean by sustainable?
If I understand you correctly, you're asking…
If I understand you correctly, you're asking about the costs.
Sorry, could you repeat the question?
Sorry, could you repeat the last part of the question?
I completely agree. / I couldn't agree more.
I couldn't agree more with that.
That's a fair point, but it's not the whole story.
I see your point, but the evidence suggests otherwise.
I'm not sure I agree with that.
I'm not sure I agree with that analysis.
I'm afraid I can't agree with you there.
I take your point; however, the cost is too high.
That may be true in the short term, but…
Up to a point. / To some extent.
I agree up to a point.
With respect, I think the figures tell a different story.
Sorry to interrupt, but could I add something?
If I could just finish my point…
If I could just finish my point, then you can respond.
That's slightly beyond the scope of my presentation.
I don't have the exact figure, but…
I don't have the exact figure, but it's around 20%.
It depends on what we mean by…
It depends on what we mean by success.
So, to answer your question, yes, but with conditions.
We'll have to agree to disagree on this one.

items: “I agree” is a verb: you do not say “I am agree”.
«In my opinion» o «I think», pero no «in my opinion I think» (redundante).
«Discuss» es transitivo: «discuss a topic», no «discuss about a topic».

ejemplos.frase: If I understand you correctly, you're asking whether the reform was necessary.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si le he entendido bien, me pregunta si la reforma era necesaria.

ejemplos.frase: That's a fair point, but it doesn't apply to small towns.
ejemplos.traduccion: Es un argumento razonable, pero no se aplica a los pueblos pequeños.

ejemplos.frase: I agree with you up to a point.
ejemplos.traduccion: Estoy de acuerdo contigo hasta cierto punto.

ejemplos.frase: Sorry to interrupt, but I think the figure is wrong.
ejemplos.traduccion: Perdona que te interrumpa, pero creo que la cifra está mal.

ejemplos.frase: We discussed the matter for hours without reaching a conclusion.
ejemplos.traduccion: Hablamos del asunto durante horas sin llegar a una conclusión.

ejemplos.frase: I'm afraid I don't have the exact figure, but I can give you an estimate.
ejemplos.traduccion: Me temo que no tengo la cifra exacta, pero puedo darle una estimación.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Agree” is a verb; it does not take “am”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: You are wrong, the data is incorrect.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: With respect, I think the data may be incorrect.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In English disagreement is softened, especially in front of an examining board.
The negative of “agree” is formed with “don't” or with “disagree”.

ejercicios.frase: I am completely agree with your analysis.
respuestas: I completely agree with your analysis.
I agree completely with your analysis.
ejercicios.explicacion: The list on this card warns: agree is a verb, not an adjective, so it does not take am. The mistake is a literal copy of the Spanish “estoy de acuerdo”. The adverb completely goes before the verb (I completely agree) or after it (I agree completely), so both versions are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Agree” is a verb: it does not take “am”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estoy completamente de acuerdo con su análisis.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I am completely agree with your analysis.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: agree is a verb and cannot go with am.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I am completely agreed with your analysis.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Be agreed exists in formal British English for groups (We are agreed), but with with your analysis the natural form is I completely agree.
Agree needs with before the person or opinion you agree with.

glosario.definicion_l: an investigation of the component parts of a whole and their relations in making up the whole · the abstract separation of a whole into its constituent parts in order to study the parts and their relations

ejercicios.frase: This afternoon we will discuss about the new budget.
respuestas: This afternoon we will discuss the new budget.
This afternoon we'll discuss the new budget.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card reminds you that discuss is transitive: you discuss something directly, without about. The mistake comes from the Spanish “hablar sobre”. The contracted form we'll is also correct, so both are accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Esta tarde hablaremos del nuevo presupuesto.

errores_previstos.respuesta: This afternoon we will discuss about the new budget.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: discuss does not take about.

errores_previstos.respuesta: This afternoon we will discuss on the new budget.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Discuss takes no preposition at all; the object follows directly.

glosario.definicion_l: a sum of money allocated for a particular purpose · a summary of intended expenditures along with proposals for how to meet them

ejercicios.frase: I couldn't agree ___. That's exactly what I think.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table lists I couldn't agree more = total agreement. Literally it means it is impossible to agree any more than you already do. The clue is the second sentence, That's exactly what I think, which confirms full agreement.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “I couldn't agree more” = I agree completely.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estoy totalmente de acuerdo. Es exactamente lo que pienso.

por_opcion.more: Correct: I couldn't agree more expresses total agreement.
por_opcion.less: Incorrect in this context: I couldn't agree less is not an established phrase and, if used, suggests disagreement.
por_opcion.better: Incorrect: agree better is not an idiomatic combination.
por_opcion.most: Incorrect: the superlative does not fit this phrase, which is comparative.

ejercicios.frase: I agree with you up to a ___, but not entirely.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives up to a point, a phrase of partial agreement. The clue is but not entirely, which qualifies the agreement. It is a fixed expression: always with a and point in the singular.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Up to a point” = partly, to some extent.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estoy de acuerdo contigo hasta cierto punto, pero no del todo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A literal copy of the Spanish “hasta cierto punto”: the fixed phrase is up to a point (or to a certain extent).
Extent existe en to some extent / to a certain extent, pero up to a extent no; con up to a va point.

glosario.definicion_l: to a complete degree or to the full or entire extent; Completely or entirely · without any others being included or involved

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the most polite option to disagree.
ejercicios.frase: ___, but I don't think the data supports that conclusion.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that in English disagreement is softened: first you concede part of the argument and then you object. I see your point is the conceding-and-objecting phrase from the table. The instruction asks for the most polite option, and the others are abrupt or colloquial.
ejercicios.traduccion: Entiendo lo que dice, pero no creo que los datos respalden esa conclusión.

por_opcion.I see your point: Correct: it concedes before objecting and is the polite way to disagree.
por_opcion.You're wrong: Grammatically possible, but too direct; the card gives it as an example of what to avoid.
por_opcion.That's nonsense: Offensive: it means that what was said is silly; unacceptable in front of an examining board.
por_opcion.No way: Colloquial and blunt (“absolutely not”); it is not polite and does not fit the structure of the sentence.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a verb (to make something clearer).
ejercicios.frase: Could you ___ what you mean by «fair taxation»?
ejercicios.explicacion: The phrase in the table for asking for clarification is Could you clarify what you mean by…? Clarify means to make a concept clearer. Explain is also accepted, as it works in the same structure, although it is more general. The clue is what you mean by, which asks for the meaning of a term to be made precise.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Podría aclarar qué quiere decir con «fiscalidad justa»?

errores_previstos.explicacion: The English verb is required: clarify.
Clear as a verb means to remove obstacles or to empty; making a concept clearer is clarify.
Explain does not take an indirect object without to (explain to me), and it is not needed here: Could you explain what you mean.

ejercicios.frase: If I understand you ___, you're asking about the long-term effects.
ejercicios.explicacion: The phrase in the table for confirming the question is If I understand you correctly. Correctly is an adverb and modifies the verb understand; hence the ending -ly. The grammatical clue is that the gap comes after a verb and an object (understand you).
ejercicios.traduccion: Si le he entendido bien, me pregunta por los efectos a largo plazo.

por_opcion.correctly: Correct: an adverb that modifies understand.
por_opcion.correct: Incorrect in careful usage: it is an adjective; although it is sometimes heard in informal speech, the phrase is correctly.
por_opcion.rightly so: Incorrect: it means “and with good reason” and does not modify understand in this structure.
por_opcion.well done: Incorrect: it is a way of congratulating someone; it does not fit.

glosario.definicion_l: relating to or extending over a relatively long time

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (to break into someone's speech).
ejercicios.frase: Sorry to ___, but could I add something?
ejercicios.explicacion: The table lists Sorry to interrupt, but… as a phrase for interrupting politely. After sorry to comes the bare infinitive: interrupt. It is spelt with a double r, as in Spanish.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Sorry to interrupt” = excuse me for interrupting.
ejercicios.traduccion: Perdone que le interrumpa, pero ¿podría añadir algo?

errores_previstos.explicacion: After sorry to comes the infinitive; sorry for interrupting also exists, but here the to is already there.
It is spelt with a double r: interrupt.

ejercicios.frase: I'm ___ I can't agree with you on that point.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives I'm afraid I can't agree as polite disagreement. I'm afraid does not express fear here: it is a polite way of introducing something negative, like the Spanish “me temo que”. The clue is can't agree, which is exactly the news being softened.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me temo que no puedo estar de acuerdo con usted en ese punto.

por_opcion.afraid: Correct: I'm afraid is a polite phrase (es: me temo que).
por_opcion.scared: Incorrect: scared expresses real fear and is not used as a polite phrase.
por_opcion.sorry of: Incorrect: you say I'm sorry, but… or I'm sorry to say, but never sorry of.
por_opcion.fear: Incorrect: fear is a verb or a noun; I'm fear is not grammatical.

ejercicios.explicacion: This is the closing phrase from the table: Does that answer your question? Answer is transitive, like discuss: you answer a question directly, without to. The clue is your question, the direct object of the verb.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A literal copy of the Spanish “responder a”: answer takes no preposition.
Respond needs to (respond to a question); this phrase uses answer.

ejercicios.frase: I'm not agree with the proposal.
respuestas: I don't agree with the proposal.
I do not agree with the proposal.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card states that the negative of agree is formed with don't (or do not) or with the verb disagree, never with am not. The three accepted answers are correct; disagree is the most direct.
ejercicios.traduccion: No estoy de acuerdo con la propuesta.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'm not agree with the proposal.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: agree is a verb and is made negative with don't.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I not agree with the proposal.
errores_previstos.explicacion: In English you need the auxiliary don't to make a present-tense verb negative.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I am disagree with the proposal.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Disagree is also a verb: I disagree, without am.

glosario.definicion_l: something proposed (such as a plan or assumption) · an offer of marriage

ejercicios.frase: That's a ___ point, but it ignores the cost.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table lists That's a fair point for conceding. Fair point means a reasonable or well-made argument; it is a fixed collocation. The clue is the structure of conceding and then objecting (but it ignores the cost).
ejercicios.traduccion: Es un argumento razonable, pero no tiene en cuenta el coste.

por_opcion.fair: Correct: a fair point = a reasonable argument.
por_opcion.just: Incorrect: just as an adjective means morally right (a just cause), but it does not collocate with point.
por_opcion.honest: Incorrect: honest applies to people or answers, not to an argument.
por_opcion.right: Incorrect: a right point is not idiomatic; you say That's right or a good point.

glosario.significado: no tener en cuenta, pasar por alto

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete the expression (leaving the disagreement aside).
ejercicios.frase: We'll have to agree to ___ on this issue.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes Let's agree to disagree for ending a disagreement in a friendly way. The fixed expression is agree to disagree: to accept that you differ. The clue is We'll have to agree to…, which can only be completed with disagree.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Agree to disagree” = accept that we do not agree.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tendremos que aceptar que no estamos de acuerdo en este asunto.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After agree to comes an infinitive, not a noun: agree to disagree.
The expression is fixed: agree to disagree.

glosario.significado: aceptar que no se está de acuerdo

glosario.definicion_l: an important question that is in dispute and must be settled · one of a series published periodically

ejercicios.explicacion: This is a polite question with a modal: Could + subject + verb + complement. The table lists it as a phrase for asking for repetition. Could goes before the subject you because it is a question.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This would be a statement or a suggestion; to ask a question, could goes before you.
The object goes after the verb: repeat the question.

ejercicios.frase: I'm afraid that question is beyond the ___ of my presentation.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives That's beyond the scope of… for limiting the answer. Scope means range or extent: beyond the scope of = outside the range of. The clue is beyond the… of my presentation, a fixed collocation that is very useful in front of an examining board.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Beyond the scope of” = outside the range of.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me temo que esa pregunta queda fuera del alcance de mi exposición.

por_opcion.scope: Correct: beyond the scope of = outside the range of.
por_opcion.scoop: Incorrect: scoop is a spoonful or a press exclusive; it only looks similar.
por_opcion.range of: Incorrect: it would repeat of (the range of of), and range does not form this collocation.
por_opcion.frame: Incorrect: frame is a physical border or structure; you would say outside the framework of, not beyond the frame of.

glosario.definicion_l: the activity of formally presenting something (as a prize or reward) · a show or display; the act of presenting something to sight or view

descripcion_larga_es: Phrases for taking part in a debate or in an examining board’s question time: asking for clarification, agreeing or disagreeing politely, conceding before objecting, qualifying, interrupting and closing an answer. This matters a great deal in an oral exam, because direct disagreement sounds abrupt in English and because there are very typical Spanish-speaker mistakes, such as “I am agree” or “discuss about”.

contexto.que_es: It is a set of functional expressions from formal spoken English: set phrases for managing the conversation in an exchange of opinions or a question session, rather than topic vocabulary.
contexto.por_que_importa: In an oral exam the board assesses both the content and the way you interact. Disagreement that is too direct can seem impolite, and not knowing how to ask for a question to be repeated leads to answering something different. In addition, mistakes such as “I am agree” are immediately perceived as basic errors.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: In debates, meetings, interviews and when defending a topic in front of an examining board. The signal is the need to react to what someone else says: confirming the question, conceding, objecting or closing. Spanish speakers tend to reply with a curt “no” or a “you are wrong”, which in English must be softened.
